summary: 1968 steel fire tower in Richmond, Rhode Island; cab gutted in a July 2022 fireworks fire; now a town radio site, with restoration or replacement disputed.

facts.design: 80-foot steel tower with a cab at the top
facts.status_note: Steel supports survived the July 2022 fire; the cab was gutted. Sources disagree on whether the old tower will be restored or replaced.

access.note: Fenced town emergency radio site. The planned compound is meant to stop people reaching the equipment by climbing the fence.

facts.agency: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management

events.note: NHLR: a tower had stood on the site since 1926, before the present one
1936 state report: tower manned as early as March 27
Lookout Mrs. Hannah Whaley spotted a fire on Orient Point, Long Island, about 40 miles away
1954-55 state report: Shannock cab had deteriorated; funds recommended for new cabs
Built field, FFLA and Westerly Sun all give 1968; NHLR's own description says 1986
Registered September 3, 2014 as US 1046, RI 7; nominated by Henry Isenberg
July 6, 2022 fireworks fire gutted the cab (NHLR gives July 7); steel supports survived per Westerly Sun
February 28, 2025: town soliciting public comment on a new 160-foot steel tower on the old site
Nov. 4 Richmond Town Council vote asks for a letter supporting restoration; article gives no year, 2025 inferred from its federal shutdown reference

corrections.why: The FFLA report says the cab was gutted by flames, and the Westerly Sun says the fire damaged the cabin but not the steel supports, so the tower itself was not destroyed. The BRVCA's 'destroyed' is looser wording.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR Built field, the FFLA report and the Westerly Sun give 1968; NHLR's own description says 1986. The record uses 1968 for the present tower. A 1954-55 state report refers to a Shannock cab, so an earlier cab existed.
The FFLA report gives July 6, 2022 and NHLR gives July 7. The record keeps July 6 and the story notes NHLR's date.
The BRVCA says the original tower was 'destroyed'; the Westerly Sun says the steel supports survived. The record follows the Westerly Sun.

notes_for_editor: Brief correction: '2022 destroyed' changed to burned (see corrections). Brief's 1968 build kept, but NHLR's description (1986) and the 1926 and 1954-55 references show the history is tangled; the story says so. Fire date: FFLA July 6 vs NHLR July 7; record uses July 6. The Westerly Sun text has no year on its 'Nov. 4' vote; 2025 is inferred from the federal shutdown reference and its sequence after the February 2025 BRVCA item. Unresolved: whether the old tower will be restored (Westerly Sun; council letter) or replaced (BRVCA). Facebook and CitizenPortal search snippets were not used as evidence. NHLR photos are not in the fetched text, so none added. Status after November 2025 is unverified. Access from the Westerly Sun: a fenced municipal radio site; no public visiting information found.
